title: Main clauses and subordinate clauses
examples: How do I write a complex sentence?

left.title: Main clause
points: Has a subject and a verb

explain.say: Think of a house and a porch. The house can stand alone, but a porch needs a house to stick onto. Sentences work the same way! Look at the left of the board: the main clause, We played cricket. It stands alone like the house.

left.title: Main clause
points: Has a subject and a verb

explain.say: Now look at the right side: when the rain stopped. Say it alone. When the rain stopped... what? It feels unfinished. That is a subordinate clause, a part that needs a main clause to lean on. Subordinate means lower in rank.

left.title: Main clause
points: Has a subject and a verb

explain.say: A clause is a group of words with a subject and a verb. See the words in the subordinate box: when, if, because. These starter words turn a clause into a leaning one. Can you spot the starter in if it is sunny?

left.title: Main clause
points: Has a subject and a verb

explain.say: Now join them: We played cricket when the rain stopped. Or flip it: When the rain stopped, we played cricket. See the board sorting starters? When the leaning part comes first, add a comma. Which order do you like?

explain.say: Excellent! A main clause plus a subordinate clause makes a complex sentence, and it makes your writing flow. Look back at the board. Challenge: add a subordinate clause to I ate a samosa. Maybe, because I was hungry?

left.title: Main clause
points: Has a subject and a verb

faq.a: A main clause has a subject and a verb and makes sense on its own, like We played cricket.
A subordinate clause has a subject and a verb but does not make sense alone. It starts with a word like when, if or because, and leans on a main clause.
A clause is a group of words with a subject and a verb. A phrase, like in the morning, has no verb.

faq.q: When do I need a comma with a subordinate clause?
faq.a: When the subordinate clause comes first, put a comma after it: Although it was late, we kept reading. When it comes second you usually need no comma.
A complex sentence has one main clause and at least one subordinate clause: I smiled because I won.

facts: Words like when, if, because and although are called subordinating conjunctions.
A clause must contain a verb; a phrase, like after lunch, does not.

quiz.say: Which part is the subordinate clause? Because she was tired, Mia went to bed.
quiz.show: Which part is the subordinate clause? Because she was tired, Mia went to bed.
quiz.why: Because she was tired cannot stand alone; it leans on the main clause.

wrong.0: This part makes sense alone, so it is the main clause.
wrong.2: This is only part of the main clause.
